name: Facet
text: Build the Excava interface in Figma as a clickable prototype first. It lets us test flows and layouts fast without coding, so we catch UX flaws early when changes cost nothing. The trade-off is we won’t see real data behavior, but that’s fine—we’re optimizing for structure and clarity first. Once the Figma prototype proves the design, we’ll swap in real data feeds with minimal rework.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A Figma prototype traps us in a static illusion—users will expect the polished mockup to match the real product, then blame us when the live tool feels sluggish or incomplete. Instead, ship a bare-bones HTML/CSS demo tonight with real API calls; it exposes real latency and data gaps now, not later. Settle this with a 30-minute sprint: build the simplest working page, then compare user reactions to the Figma version—if the live one scores worse on clarity or enjoyment, we pivot back to Figma.

name: Facet
text:
Ship a live HTML/CSS prototype tonight with real API calls. It forces us to face real latency, data gaps, and edge cases now—before users do—so we can tune performance and content before polishing. The trade-off is rougher visuals and slower iteration than Figma, but we’ll catch deal-breakers the mockup hides. Once the core works, we’ll layer in the Figma polish without redoing the foundation.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A live HTML/CSS demo tonight risks shipping a fragile artifact that looks broken to stakeholders—real latency exposes gaps, but also makes the *tool* the story, not the *interface*. Instead, run a 2-hour "smoke test" with real API calls in a stripped-down Figma frame: users click buttons, see loading states, but the frame itself stays polished. Settle it by timing how long it takes to mock the API response in Figma versus debugging a half-baked demo tomorrow.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: Ship a live, minimal HTML/CSS demo of Excava’s core flow with mocked API data by tonight—visibility into real latency and data gaps without exposing stakeholders to a fragile tool. Owned by Pane.
